measurements.name: core-trustworthiness fixtures (Rust + Python, synthetic, dynamic-probe-verified)
measurements.unknown_total_vs_declared_note: unknown_total_count equals unknown_count (11) here because each fixture project is an isolated checkout containing only that fixture's own files — the declared universe and the whole graph's discovered universe are the same closed set. This is NOT true for the representative-mutations measurement below (Click is a real repository).

measurements.name: core-representative-mutations (Click 8.4.1, real repository, one declared dynamic-dispatch mutation)
measurements.offline_source: pinned cache .benchmark-cache/core-representative-v1/918b5633eddf6b41c32d4f454bf0de810065c74e3f7dbf8ee5452f8be88d3e96.tar.gz, sha256-verified against docs/core-representative-corpus.json before use; no network fetch performed
measurements.flat_aggregate_note: This 0.000 recall on the flat/legacy mechanism is the pre-existing, already-documented dynamic-dispatch gap (docs/core-representative-mutations.md); unchanged by Stage 1 work.
measurements.unknown_total_vs_declared_note: unknown_total_count (472) is Click's true discovered Unknown-test count across its whole indexed test suite; unknown_count (3) is that narrowed to only the three tests this mutation declares. The gap (469 tests) is real: this measurement says nothing about them, and a naive read of only unknown_count would understate how much of Click's suite this graph currently cannot exclude for ANY change, not just this one.

trustworthy_must_gate.criterion: precision 1.000 with a nonempty Must set and zero false Must claims
trustworthy_must_gate.reason: Must set is empty on every corpus measured (synthetic fixtures and the one real-repository mutation); precision is therefore undefined (null), not met. May is empty in every case too (0.000 recall wherever a positive existed) because the extractor does not yet enumerate any May candidates at all.

root_causes_observed: Cross-file calls cannot reach Must: annotate() (crates/aether-builder/src/mapper/claims.rs) runs once per file during extraction, before project-wide resolve_calls, so a call's target must be declared in the SAME file's syntax tree to be provable. Verified directly against the fixture layout (find fixtures/core-trustworthiness -type f): both the Rust and Python trustworthiness fixtures' tests live in a different file from the function they cover (tests/impact.rs vs src/operations.rs; tests/test_service.py vs models.py), and Click's declared mutation (Group.invoke in src/click/core.py) is called from tests/test_commands.py and tests/test_chain.py.

Python and (by the same top-level-only rule) any other language's test METHODS on a class cannot reach Must even when same-file: the extractor's proof rule only walks direct children of the module root (or an export_statement at that level), not class/impl-body methods. Click and the trustworthiness Python fixture both declare tests as methods (OracleTests::test_*, and Click's pytest-style module-level functions are the exception that does qualify structurally, but still fails on the cross-file rule above).

The extractor never emits CallClass::May: it has no enumeration logic yet for trait objects, generics, interface implementors, overloads, inheritance, or structural typing (Stage 3 work, per docs/roadmap.md); every non-Must call site is currently classified Unknown rather than May.

classified_impact's flood rule (aether-graph/src/claims.rs) marks every Function node in the WHOLE graph as at least Unknown once a single Unknown-classified call exists anywhere in the graph, not just near the queried origin — so on any real codebase the practical result is close to 'everything is at least Unknown, at minimum'. This is what makes unknown_total_count (472 on Click) so much larger than any single query's declared-relevant set (3).
limitations: Only Rust and Python fixtures are exercised by core-trustworthiness; the corpus has no TypeScript or Go cases yet, so this measurement says nothing about those two languages' Must/May behavior.

core-representative-mutations has exactly one declared mutation (group-invoke) against one repository (Click); it is evidence that the dynamic comparison harness runs end-to-end against real code, not a general accuracy claim (see docs/core-gap-analysis.md's own framing, unchanged here).

This is not yet the dedicated dispatch corpus Stage 2 requires (40+ cases weighted to trait objects/generics/inheritance/structural typing/interfaces); it is the existing mutation corpus named in Stage 1's precommitted criterion.

The boundary flood makes Unknown counts and boundary counts a property of the whole indexed graph, not a tight measure of origin-local uncertainty; docs/roadmap.md records this as a named consequence, not a hidden one.

classified_impact(&[]) (an origin set with no function nodes, e.g. a const-only or type-only edit) returns empty with no boundary notice at all — not measured here, but named as a known gap in docs/roadmap.md.
